newsitem.title: POLAND: OTC launch seen as boost to Polish capital market.
newsitem.headline: OTC launch seen as boost to Polish capital market.

text.p: Poland's OTC market, set for launch in late October, will help the young capital market grow by offering investment alternatives and attracting new investors, the head of a firm set up to run the market said.
Czeslaw Gawlowski, president of Centralna Tabela Ofert (CeTO), told Reuters in an interview on Wednesday he hoped the market would attract capital from the Warsaw bourse and also new investors.
"It's an enrichment of the Polish capital market, so far not accessible for many firms and many investors. Access to the Polish securities market is becoming broader," Gawlowski said.
He said many speculators were likely to switch from the bourse to the OTC market (CTO) as the latter, much more risky and speculative, would offer more opportunities for fast and large profits.

"We expect a significant number of short-term investors to move to CTO, as they will be able to trade continuously with no price limits in stocks that will give them a chance to make money quickly, but we also hope medium-term investors will come," he said.

Trading will be carried out from Monday to Friday, from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. local time. CTO will have ITO index (Index Tabeli Ofert) for stocks and other indices will be created later for bonds, stocks sectors and others.
Gawlowski added that he believed institutional investors might also see an oppotyunity in investing in small cap but potentially fast-growing firms, which he hoped would enter CTO.

"Our financial market is very shallow and when funds such as pension funds start existing, they will have to invest diversifying their portfolio, so some of the capital will certainly flow to CTO," he said.

Gawlowski said he believed many prospective companies would prefer to enter CTO rather than the free market of the bourse, because the requirements and costs were much lower while access to capital was similar.

"We hope there will be small firms from such sectors as electronics, biotechnology and sophisticated chemical industry applying; they are often not such big firms, but they have very significant growth potential," he said.

So far only insurance company Polisa SA, which also wants to enter the bourse, has applied for CTO listing. A machine tool maker Rafamet SA, which is seeking Polish Securities Commission approval for public trading, also wants to trade on the CTO.
Gawlowski said he expected more companies to apply after the treasury ministry makes available funds to help companies prepare simplified issue prospectuses, necessary to float the shares.
He said CeTo needed several large firms to be listed or more than a hundred small companies to become profitable.
Gawlowski said besides stocks CTO would list bonds, and would also consider trading in derivatives, but it was difficult to say when that would be possible.
